newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Pacific selling Marathon unit.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific selling Marathon unit.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd said on Friday it was selling its Marathon Realty Company Ltd and Centrixx Realty Holdings Ltd units to Oxford Properties Group Inc and General Electric Capital Corp.
Canadian Pacific said the sale of the Marathon portfolio would be completed at a price of about C$952 million including assumed debt.

The Montreal-based conglomerate said it would sell the Marathon portfolio to a newly incorporated company that will be owned equally by Oxford and GE Capital, a unit of General Electric Co. The Marathon portfolio includes about 12 million square feet of office and retail properties in Canada.
Canadian Pacific said the agreement excluded Marathon's U.S. retail assets and land and development sites.

Oxford said it would manage the properties and expected to employ most of the Marathon employees now overseeing the properties. GE Capital Canada Inc. would provide a first mortgage financing facility, the companies said.
"This acquisition will nearly double Oxford's asset base, and will extend the company's property management business to 45 million square feet" said Oxford chief executive Jon Love in a statement.
Canadian Pacific chief executive David O'Brien said in a statement that the sale of the real estate assets would enable it to focus resources on its transportation, energy and hotel businesses.
